Ten problems across the three new files: 3 errors and 7 warnings.

All three files are untracked, so they were reviewed in full. To run the linters I installed the JS dev dependencies with `npm ci`, which brought in oxlint. ruff has no Python lockfile in the project, so I ran the version pinned in `pyproject.toml` with `uvx ruff@0.17.1`, without installing it.

```
Code standards: uncommitted changes, 3 files, 2.1s (ast-grep 0.5s, lizard 0.05s, jscpd 2.1s, oxlint 1.3s, ruff via uvx)

Errors
  app/api/loyalty_routes.py
    10  cs-env-outside-config     os.environ.get("LOYALTY_RATE", ...): read it from app.config.settings instead; only app/config.py reads the environment
  web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx
    10  eslint(no-debugger)       stray `debugger;` left in the render body   [fix]
  app/services/loyalty_service.py
     1  ruff F401                 `json` is imported but never used   [fix]

Warnings
  app/api/loyalty_routes.py
    11  std-routes-delegate       the handler calls get_db().fetch_one(...) itself; pass get_db() to a service call instead
    12  std-routes-delegate       a missing customer returns {"points": 0}; it should raise LookupError in the service so the route gives a 404
    14  std-routes-delegate       the gold-tier rate doubling is business logic in the handler, and points_for also adds a gold bonus (line 16), so gold logic lives in two places
  app/services/loyalty_service.py
     9  std-service-errors        find_customer returns None for a missing customer (and is typed `dict | None`); raise LookupError(f"customer {customer_id} not found")
    13  lizard/complexity         points_for: complexity 11 (limit 10); the tier if/elif chain could become a lookup table
  web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx
     6  std-components-use-api-modules  calls fetch() directly; add getLoyalty(id) to web/src/api/customer.ts and use it
    14  lizard/complexity         summarize: complexity 12 (limit 10)
    14  jscpd/duplicate           summarize copies web/src/components/InvoiceList.tsx:24-35 (12 lines); move it to web/src/lib/format.ts and import it in both
```

The three route warnings share one fix:
- **Rewrite the route:** have `show_loyalty` make a single call, e.g. `loyalty_service.points_for_customer(get_db(), id)`.
- **Move the logic into the service:** that function looks up the customer with `find_customer` (which would raise `LookupError` once fixed), reads the rate from settings, and applies the gold-tier rule in one place.
- **Unused function:** right now `find_customer` is defined but nothing calls it.

I can apply the two `[fix]` items now (remove `debugger` and the unused import), and the refactors above if you want them.
